question.problem: If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ drawn from a population with mean $\mu =24$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$  determine the smallest sample size required so that the standard error of the mean is less than $0.5.$
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}
$$

Since the population standard deviation is $\sigma =\sqrt{1}=1,$ we have that 

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We require that the standard error is less than $0.5.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} & <0.5 \\ \sqrt{n} & >\frac{1}{0.5} \\ \sqrt{n} & >2 \\ n & >{2}^{2} \\ n & >4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest sample size is $n=5.$
